The June 13, 2018 FOMC statement is moderately hawkish and economically upbeat: it reports “solid” activity, “strong” job gains, unemployment falling, and inflation near 2%, and it signals “further gradual increases” in the federal funds rate while noting balanced risks. This guidance aligns with rule-like behavior documented in the monetary-policy literature: Clarida, Galí, and Gertler’s estimates of Fed reaction functions and Taylor-type rules imply rate hikes when inflation is near/at target and resource utilization is strong, with interest-rate smoothing favoring gradualism. The emphasis on a “symmetric” 2% objective and little-changed long-term expectations is consistent with inflation-forecast targeting principles (Svensson and Woodford), helping mitigate average inflation bias and time-inconsistency concerns by anchoring expectations. On implementation, raising IOER to 1.95% and setting ON RRP at 1.75% to keep market rates within the 1.75–2.00% target fits modern operating frameworks discussed by Goodfriend, using administered rates to steer the funds rate in a reserves-abundant environment. Continued balance-sheet runoff and strong business investment further reinforce a normalization stance; the absence of highlighted financial stress reduces the need for risk-management dovishness often implied by financial-accelerator models (Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist). Net tone: positive on growth and employment with measured hawkishness on policy normalization.
